page: Microsoft Azure F4als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated physical cores delivering 4 vCPUs at 1 thread per core. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support including AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, and AVX-512_BF16) alongside AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-threaded compute efficiency. The instance achieved top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core performance (3081.08) and Geekbench single-core execution (2087.0), complemented by solid text processing throughput. Multi-core performance aligns within average industry percentiles, posting 12288.15 in stress-ng multi-core and 6710.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests. While small-block cached read bandwidth is substantial at 591.29 GB/sec, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is constrained at 36.2 GB/sec, placing its PassMark memory profile in the lower quartile. Redis operations reach 10.41 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measures 8.24 GB/sec.

With its dedicated core allocation and compact 8.0 GB memory footprint, the F4als_v6 provides a cost-efficient resource tier for workloads that prioritize raw CPU cycles over high RAM density or persistent local disk IOPS. The absence of local disk requires external networked storage configurations for stateful applications. The instance is best suited for CI/CD software compilation, CPU-bound batch processing, static web hosting, and lightweight machine learning inference tasks with small parameter models.
